rationale: Joint distributed rewrite of the only editable communication boundary: the single c10d.allreduce_ dispatch target through which the frozen step issues its entire 13-collective gradient synchronization (inputs/targets.json: d0938de87369efd500322679 = 12 buckets of 7,087,872 fp32 elements = 28,351,488 B; b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b = the is-last embedding bucket of 39,385,344 elements = 157,541,376 B; inputs/groups.json maps each selected group to exactly these calls). DDP parameters, payload bytes and the frozen adapter are invariants, so the only movable term in the objective is the device waiting that the project's own caveat says is included in NCCL kernel durations (inputs/source/workloads.json communication_metric_caveat: 'Includes device waiting; is not wire time, critical-path time or exposed communication'). Mechanism: each replacement first meets both ranks at one CPU-side gloo rendezvous -- reusing the gloo control group the frozen adapter already creates outside timing in prepare() and already uses for pre-step barriers in before_run() -- and only then calls the parent c10d::allreduce_ op through context.references with identical tensors, process group 0, ReduceOp.SUM and async semantics. A gloo barrier enqueues no CUDA kernel, so it cannot add to communication_kernel_sum_ms; it moves each rank's submission instant to common ground so the peer spin-wait leaves the NCCL kernels. Both call IDs are replaced together because 13 dispatches share one target: aligning a subset would leave the remaining dispatches staggered and the first-arrival wait pattern intact. Evidence: (1) inputs/project.json original_baseline diagnostics: clean objective samples rank 0 = 62.08-63.14 ms (at the aligned-submission reference scale, waiting for nobody) while rank 1 = 83.72-86.99 ms and sets the 86.48 ms objective, i.e. ~21-24 ms of excess wait on the early rank; step_ms baseline 141.2/141.3 ms gives the 1.05x budget of ~148.4 ms. (2) inputs/observations/current/execution_timeline-1221e205.json cross_rank.collectives sequences 21-33: per-collective cpu_submit_spread_bounds_us of 14,865-16,014 us on every one of the 13 matched allreduces in an instrumented run; that file's own scope states it measures CPU submission spread with monotonic-bound alignment, 'not GPU arrival skew or transport duration'. (3) inputs/observations/current/nsys-9ed9145c.json: separate nsys capture of the same shape -- rank 0 nccl_kernel_sum_ms 280.28 with the first kernel absorbing ~220 ms of waiting, rank 1 at 63.98 ms; its scope forbids cross-rank timestamp subtraction, so it corroborates wait absorption under instrumentation, not clean-run timing. (4) inputs/target-resources.json: rank-local durations of the same capture -- rank 1 43,893.81 us over the 12 small kernels (~3.66 ms each, matching the aligned reference) and 19,536.7 us for the single large kernel, versus rank 0 261,744.8 us for the same 12; the recorded launch registers/shared memory are launch configuration, not occupancy, hardware traffic or causal effects. Evidence-reading check on synthetic calibration: inputs/observations/current/collective_calibration-1af5837f.json measures correctness-checked synthetic contiguous allreduces at the exact observed sizes/dtypes/world size -- median 3.55-3.63 ms per 28,351,488 B bucket and 19.40-19.70 ms for 157,541,376 B -- and its interpretation field states it is a synthetic reference at observed payload size, 'not a reproduction of model scheduling or a lower bound', that its logical payload rate 'is not busbw or wire throughput', and that no model critical-path savings may be inferred. This proposal therefore uses those numbers only as a scale reference for near-aligned submissions on this transport; it does not claim they are pure transfer time, a critical-path lower bound, or GPU-ready skew. GPU arrival skew and hardware traffic were not measured (nsys hardware_traffic_status 'unknown'; timeline clock_policy forbids cross-rank timestamp arithmetic); the achievable objective floor after rendezvous is unknown until the framework's paired revalidation measures it, and selection.json's -21% to -26% estimate remains a hypothesis. Why step_ms should hold: the ~15-24 ms skew is slack on the early rank; the rendezvous burns it as a CPU-side gloo wait on that rank while its already-enqueued backward work drains, instead of as GPU spin inside its NCCL kernels. The late (pacing) rank arrives at each barrier last and pays only the barrier round-trip (~0.1-0.3 ms x13, inside the ~148.4 ms budget vs 141.3 ms baseline). No CUDA work is added or removed; the final allreduce still starts when the late rank's backward finishes and completes ~19.5 ms later on both ranks, so the completion boundary and optimizer ordering are unchanged. Numerics and state: the parent op performs the identical in-place reduction on identical operands over the same communicator with the same stream ordering; reduction results are timing-invariant, so loss, gradients and parameters stay within the frozen 1e-6/1e-4 tolerances (expected bit-identical). The gloo rendezvous carries no payload, touches no model state and mirrors the source's existing out-of-band control-group usage; it adds no group-0 collective, so collective_identity, logical_payload and cross_rank_collectives should still see the same 13 payload-identical matched NCCL allreduces. Route reporting distinguishes 'gloo-rendezvous+parent-nccl', 'fallback:signature-mismatch' (unsupported signature -> parent), 'fallback:no-rendezvous-group' (setup failure -> parent) and 'fallback:barrier-error' (runtime rendezvous failure -> parent). Guards check cross-rank-identical properties (single 1-D contiguous fp32 CUDA tensor with the site's observed numel and null sparse_indices), so both ranks always take the same path and collective participation is preserved; the 30 s barrier timeout sits below the 120 s NCCL process-group timeout and the 900 s worker timeout, and any barrier failure degrades to the unmodified parent rather than breaking numerics. No inputs/previous-candidate or inputs/previous-feedback.txt exists for this selection, so this is the first attempt at the selected hypothesis.

setup_work.build_time: No GPU work, no tensor allocation, no process-group creation, no comm hook, no graph capture: build() only reads state['control'] (the gloo control group the frozen adapter already created outside timing in prepare()), binds the current parent callables from context.references, and installs two callables.
setup_work.first_invocation: Each guarded call executes one dist.barrier on the existing gloo control group (timeout 30 s) before dispatching the parent op; the first rendezvous executes inside the first real workload invocation (warmup runs precede measured repeats), so no setup lands inside a measured step.
setup_work.memory: No new CUDA allocations and no retained pools; CUDA allocator counters (peak_allocated/reserved and lifecycle peaks) are unaffected. The gloo barrier is CPU/socket-side only and reports no CUDA or NCCL kernel.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: The replacements are stateless with respect to model/optimizer state; reset() and the warm-model lifecycle are untouched, and the control group is used strictly sequentially (before_run barrier on the main thread, then the 13 in-run rendezvous on the dispatching autograd thread).

quality_risks: If any framework phase ever dispatched these sites asymmetrically across ranks, the gloo rendezvous could stall up to its 30 s timeout before degrading to the parent; the guards only accept cross-rank-identical properties (targets.json shows identical shapes, dtypes and counts on ranks 0 and 1), so both ranks take the same path on every invocation.
Rendezvous failures (timeout, gloo error) fall back to the unmodified parent NCCL call with route 'fallback:barrier-error'; numerics never depend on the rendezvous succeeding.

If clean-run skew is dominated by one-time first-kernel absorption rather than per-collective stagger, the gain shrinks toward removing only that absorption; the instrumented execution_timeline shows per-collective spread on all 13 sequences, but clean runs cannot distinguish the two (selection.json unknowns), so the realized improvement is bounded by the paired revalidation.

step_ms risk: blocking the early rank's CPU at each barrier could drain its GPU queue; budget is ~148.4 ms (1.05x of 141.3 ms baseline) against an expected per-call barrier overhead of ~0.1-0.3 ms x13 on the pacing rank; the step_ms <= 1.05x constraint is enforced independently.

cross_rank_collectives matching must still pair the 13 allreduces; the rendezvous adds no group-0 collective and changes no payload, and it reuses the source's own out-of-band control-group pattern, but the observation must confirm matching is undisturbed by the compressed submission times.

The held-out longer_sequence workload (sequence_length 256) produces different bucket sizes; the guards then route to the parent with no rendezvous, so no deadlock or regression is introduced there, and the optimization simply does not apply.

All 13 NCCL allreduces still execute via context.references (nothing eliminated), so runtime coverage counts real replacement invocations and real parent calls; no attempt is made to substitute the collectives themselves.
